sections.content:
MATH1013 is the standard Calculus I for students with DSE M1/M2 background. It teaches single-variable calculus: limits, continuity, derivatives and basic integrals. The lecturer delivers lectures logically with neat board notes. The pace is appropriate and examples help clarify abstract theories.
Assessments: homework, quizzes, midterm and final. Grading is fair. Workload is acceptable if you finish weekly practice. Students with DSE M2 knowledge can handle this course comfortably.
sections.teaching: The lecturer explains calculus concepts logically. Board notes are neat and easy to follow. Lecture pace is suitable, and illustrative examples help understand abstract theories clearly.
sections.grading: The lecturer explains calculus concepts logically. Board notes are neat and easy to follow. Lecture pace is suitable, and illustrative examples help understand abstract theories clearly.
sections.workload: Medium workload. Keeping up with weekly homework and practice problems is enough to stay on track.

sections.content: I honesty don't understand why this course is 4 credits. It's literally ISOM 2500 all over again. It covers probability, linear regression with single and multiple regressor, inferential statistics regarding these regressions and non linear regression. The course is very application focused most of the work is analyzing the regression examples of real life topics.
sections.teaching: I think it's average. The lesson is on 9a.m. so I skipped half the lectures. I self studied most of the course
sections.grading: The grade is mostly on exams, along with 4 assignments and 5% on discussion. For the discussion bit you have to attend lectures and answer his questions (the prof will discuss questions on the textbook in class). To get all 5% you have to answer 5 times. The assignment is where I think everyone got full mark. I got 1 s.d. in midterm but did bad in the finals (37/55, they did not release the distribution) and got B+.
sections.workload: For a 4 credit course the workload is incredibly low. The 4 assignments are easy. The only workload is revising for exams.

sections.content:
Module 0: Introduction econometrics
Module 1: Review of probability
Module 2: Review of statistics
Module 3: Linear regression with a single regressor: Estimation
Module 4: Linear regression with a single regressor: Characterization
Module 5: Linear regression with a single regressor: Inference
Module 6: Linear regression with multiple regressors: Estimation
Module 7: Linear regression with multiple regressors: Inference
Module 8: Instrumental variable regression with a single regressor: Binary instrument
Module 9: Instrumental variable regression with a single regressor and a single instrument
Module 10: Instrumental variable regression with multiple regressors and multiple instruments
It should follow the content of the book Stock and Watson.

It is hard to decide on the grading.
There is a LOTTTTT of content covered in his lecture. If you are a passionate learner, this course should be an interesting one for you.
Before the midterm, it should be better as it is more about probability and statistics, especially when you have taken DSE M1 (but actually, previous knowledge on M1 just makes it easier for you to digest the content. M1 focus 99% on calculation, but Prof. Huang emphasizes a lot on CONCEPT. There is nearly no calculation needed in the exam). Not sure if ISOM2500 has the same effect because I didn't put much effort into that course.
After the midterm, it is quite horrible. It is all about linear regression. And in my opinion, courses like ISOM2500 and ISOM2600 don't help much with it. Cause these two courses just give you a brief idea of what linear regression  and some formulas (e.g. R-squared and adjusted R-squared) are, but linear regression is more complicated then you imagine...
However, I feel like this course is occupying all my studying time (due to my poor time management), and I crashed out a few times while revising it. And as I put too much focus on this course, I failed to prepare myself adequately for the finals of other courses. So, if you are going to take this course, please make sure to plan your time wisely and start your revision earlier.
If you don't have much time, SKIP ALL MATH-RELATED PART during your own revision. They help, but are not necessary in this course.
But once you understand the concept thoroughly, you will be fine.
sections.teaching:
Very very very nice and open-minded prof. His teaching is indeed clear to understand. For me, I suggest you to attend his lectures/ watch his recordings to understand things more clearly. He answers emails quickly, and that really helps a lot. And he is quite fun. (He likes to make jokes during lesson, although some of them sounds bit 'kam', haha)

TA should be a nice guy too, but if you attend his tutorial, he will keep walking around the classroom and ask questions

sections.workload: If I have to grade it in terms of the amount of homework, then it is an A. However, as the content is so dense, you need to put a lot of effort in revision.

sections.content:
1. Introduction to econometrics (causal inference, randomized experiments)
2. Review of probability (probability, random variables, moments, distributions, law of iterated expectations, variance and independence)
3. Review of statistics (Finite sample analysis, interval estimation, hypothesis testing, asymptotic analysis)
4. linear regression (I) (LR for prediction, causal inference, parameter estimation, classical LR assumptions)
5. Linear regression (II) (Multivariate linear regression, F-test, heterogeneity, time series)
6. Instrumental variables regression
sections.teaching: Professor Huang is a very kind and patient instructor. He uploads all lecture recordings, hand-written notes during class and other relevant materials on canvas. I would say his teaching is rigorous and exquisite, if you are interested in econometrics or statistics you would be amazed by the complex derivations and mathematical proofs. Though proofs and derivations are mostly not examined, they provide good intuition in understanding the underlying working principle. He really did put effort in his teaching and explanation during class (very rare in UST), which is very respectable and appreciated in my opinion. You should take this course when you see Prof Huang lol.
sections.grading:
I must say that the grading under professor Huang is one of the best I have ever seen.
Assessment breakdown:
20% HW (4 problem sets)
30% midterm
50% final
The midterm is extremely easy since the mean is 51.7/60, so it basically does not differentiate students at all. All 4 assignments are graded by effort (basically free 20%). However, the final exam is extremely hard in my opinion (understandable because students have to be differentiated eventually). Honestly speaking I did very poorly in the final exam (speculated at least 30 marks gone off after exam, out of 100) and I think I would get a B+ at most (despite scoring 58/60 in the midterm, but again it doesn't mean anything). However I received an A at last (final marks and statistics not released). It really shows how lenient prof Huang is as I totally do not deserve such a nice letter grade.
sections.workload: The workload is very small since you only have to complete 4 problem sets throughout the entire semester. All problems sets are quoted from the textbook directly. I personally think problem sets do not serve as good reference to the exams since exams are basically about intuitions and explanations while most problem set questions are pure calculations. Maybe it is due the fact that prof Huang is a "newbie" in UST haha.

sections.content:
Introductory econometrics. Find the details in attached syllabus. Given the time limit, the prof give up the last 2 modules, so I think the contents this semester is easier than regular contents.

There is one application module not shown in syllabus, where he teaches how to read and explain the data forms in emperical papers. This part is very useful and instructive for very basic paper reading.

According to previous 3334 syllabus, I have expected something on R programming before semester. However, he only shows us some codes screenshots and no need to actually learn how to do coding work. This also makes the contents much easier. Generally, the difficulty seems much lower than normal 4 credits major requirement courses.
sections.teaching:
emm...

The lecture was very detailed and easy to follow up, but sometimes is quite boring. He showed us the very basic logics of different methods, which is very useful for understanding.

However, his accents may make it confusing.

Very patient to answer questions.

However, considering his participation part of grading scheme, students need to ask 5 questions in class to ensure a full score. Then people may ask some very very basic questions or just ask for concept repeating or clarification, which may be a waste of time. So he spent 3 weeks to finish the first module "review for statistics", and only finished 3 modules before the midterm exam. It is hard to give evaluation.
sections.grading:
What a gooooood grade!!! I have never known that the grading scheme in hkust can be so great.

He uses absolute grading, with the cutoffs of A, B, C and D range being 85, 70, 50 and 40 respectively.

In class discussion (participation) 10%
Problem sets 30%
Midterm 30%
Final 30%

It's easy to get a full score in class participation, only need to ask in total 5 questions in class and post them on discord. No actual "attendance".
Problem sets are also easy. Multiple choice questions are easy, and some mathematical justification questions need some basic logic work. But some long questions need very detailed explanations, and may be hard to get full scores.

Midterm and final both have only 30 total scores, which means that if you lose a point in the exam, you will lose a point in the overall score. This is quite anxious, but the exams are not difficult if you follow his lectures.

Maybe this he’s not really suitable for this class, but I still rate his teaching B because he is really a good guy—so kind a person that I can guarantee that he must be a good husband and a good dad in his family life. As long as you don’t understand something and could explain your question clearly, he is always ready to answer you both in-class and after class. sections.content:
The target of this course is how to study a causal effect of a treatment on the dependent variable.

1. Introduction
2. Probability Review
3. Statistics Review
Some of the things are not covered in Math2411/2421, and he will also introduce some terminology that are useful in this course, so don't skip it.

4. Linear Regression on Single Regressor
5. Robust Standard Error
6. Control Variables and Multiple Regressors
7. F-test
8. Application
Some real world examples are given.
9. Advanced Methods
Heterogeneous Causal Effects, Instrumental Variables, Difference-in-Differences.

This course focus on
1) the correctness of the model
2) the math part (inference step)

I would say wang peng put a lot of emphasis on the first part. In the final exam part 2 (56/100), there are a lot of these kinds of philosophical question:
- If the data generation process is like this, can we say that some population parameter is independent of another population parameter?
- Under different data generation process, can we believe that the OLS estimator is correctly describing the causal effect?

These questions are very hard to answer (or even search in net I think), it really test your understanding on the material of this course and how carefully you can think of to make sure the models are correct. It often requires insights on real life situation. Therefore, even you are good at the Math part, you still have to understand the art of Econometrics to ace this course (when Wang Peng is teaching).

I would say this arrangement is reasonable because an incorrect model leads to incorrect inference. The math part can be solved by machines easily today. So the job of Economists is to define a correct model. Actually, I appreciate such kind of art/philosophy of Econometrics.
sections.teaching:
Wang Peng is a very nice, kind gentleman, and he tries to provide as much help as possible to students.

I would say his teaching is quite good but the design of the content of lecture notes is bad.

Let's talk about his verbal delivery first. His English is quite good with light accent. One problem is that he never stress some points, meaning that he speaks everything at similar tone. He will speak the mathematical formulas directly which is difficult to listen to, e.g. variance of sum equals to sum of variance plus 2 times covariances. Luckily I got Zoom this year so that I can replay. Besides these things, I think his explanations are quite good.

But the flow of lecture notes is very bad.
Since I take Math2411 before and get destroyed by ycw. I really appreciate that the review part make me understand a lot more compared in Math2411.
However, starting at chapter 4, I lose my mind of the sudden change of topic. It is like I haven't attend to class for few weeks. A lot of notations that are quite confusing and some math equations that jumps out from nowhere.
For example, the average treatment effect E(Y_{1i} - Y_{0i}) is very confusing. I originally thought it is for a single person but it is actually the average effect on the whole population.
Another example: the mean independence requirement for OLS model: E(u|X) = 0 jumps out from nowhere. I can fully understand it after the chapter of control variables. It is used to prevent the "selection bias", meaning say people choosing particular treatment X may tends to have certain characteristics that affect our results.

I guess he intended to teach us all the theory part first, then it will be much easier (he thought) to learn to subsequent content. For example, in the first few slides of chapter 4, there is a slide talking about heterogeneous variance population model. It will be used in ch5 and ch9 later but he decided to put it earlier. That makes the lecture notes very difficult to understand as some slides are actually for more advanced topics.

Therefore, I am super confused in chapter 4 and everything gets clear after the whole chapter 6. You will understand more why he put a slide before when the course progress.

His lecture notes is not enough for revision, go to lesson and jot down some explanations or you will confused yourself through self-learning his notes.

After the mid term, things are getting more difficult. But wp is willing teach much slower when I reported to him that we don't understand the lectures. He also spend the last two lectures on reviewing the final exam, so make sure you attend his last two lectures.

I know some students are complaining about the content is not enough, it looks like a 3-credit course rather than 4 credit.
sections.teaching:
I studied with 3 of econ and ecof friends. All of us think that his teaching is exceptionally good.
If you are econ students, you should take his course. You will learn a lot of advanced regression techniques (useful in modelling trend like stock and index).

He provides detailed and clear explanation on different concepts. Students with only ISOM2500 background (like me) also can get a good grade in his course, you just need to understand his teaching materials (lecture notes + what he said in class)

If you cannot catch up, you can watch his lecture video. He is very kind and provide all lecture videos on canvas.
sections.grading:
20% homework
25% mid term
55% final

your input to the course is highly correlated to your scores in mid term and final:
corr(input(in hours), scores)=0.9!

I studied for a few days before the final and mid term, turn out my result was not that bad.

mid term score 19.5/25, above mean ~1sd
final exam score above mean ~0.5sd

turnout A-

my friends also got a range.
sections.workload:
5 assignments throughout the whole semester. If you know how to google, you can survive. Light workload.
Remember to spend some time before final exam, because most of the questions are based on textbook examples.

sections.content: Basically about probability, statistics, regression (linear and nonlinear), STATA. If you have taken related Math course or ISOM course before, then this course will be relatively easy.
sections.teaching: Professor LU Xun is a quite patient and nice person. He focuses on the concept and derivation of the formulas. Although the speed might be a little bit slow, overall the teaching well explains the basic knowledge of Econometrics.
sections.grading: Quite satisfactory. Homework problems are simple and straightforward, everybody can get a full mark on that. Midterms and final exams are relatively easy since you can bring cheat sheet and most problems are actually simple Math problems.
sections.workload: Not much. About seven easy homework, one midterm and final. But you do need to listen carefully and fully grasp the logic of knowledge. It would be better if you read the textbook and try to practice exercises after each chapter. Further more, you can try to derive the formula by yourself.

sections.content:
Starting from reviewing stuffs in introductory statistics, then move on to multiple regressions, non-linear regression.

Although the first part is review, more proofs are introduced than introductory level. I think those content are more difficult than the latter part.

The latter part can be digged into very deeap, but as we focus on application more, those difficult math are not covered. As a result, we are just substituting numbers into equations with a basic understanding towards the concepts.
sections.teaching:
He teaches very well. Everything are explained clearly with easy examples. His teaching pace is very slow which makes everything pleasing. He will go through all the slides with you, so attending lesson helps shorten your revision time.

Also, he understands that some of us are not really good at maths, he try to focus on the concept and application. But for sure maths cannot be avoided.
sections.grading:
15% HW
30% midterm
55% final

The grading is fair in Econ deparment. Do not trust some sayings that he is strict in giving grades.

Scoring average in midterm is fine, you can catch up in final.
sections.workload:
6 homework (5 counted)
Mt
Final

The midterm requires proof and is very long. I’d say it is quite difficult too. Many students cannot finish the paper. This leads the a 5x% mean.

For final, due to the nature of content, it is mich simpler. We are given 3 hours to finish but many leave after 2 hours. Mean is around 80%.

sections.content:
The contents are pretty much summarized in the course description.

Topics included in this course:
Nonlinear Regression Functions
Linear Regression with One Regressor
Regression with a Single Regressor:
Hypothesis Tests and Confidence Intervals
Linear Regression with Multiple Regressors
etc.
sections.teaching: the lectures are boring, if you are not good at statistics, better learn it yourself before going to class.
sections.grading:
poor grading,
The average grade is C as i heard from!
sections.workload:
only 4 assignments throughout the semester , you can get the answer from google search
Lectures and tutorials are optional. No attendance will be taken.

sections.content: Some basic knowledge which is a bit further than MATH2411. It's somehow an introductory course about econometrics.
sections.teaching: He teaches the material at very low speed. Therefore, his class is easy to understand but boring.
sections.grading: If you attend every lecture and tutorial, finish the homework and stata lab, things will become very easy. One important thing is, the tutorial is very important, which is even more important than lecture. If you unfortunately miss a tutorial, you'd better manage to catch up with the stuff taught in the tutorial.
sections.workload: Things are easy but the revision is necessary. The workload is not heavy.

sections.content:
Clear notes to introduce the basic probability review, hypothesis testing and various regression model.
The most important topic is regression model. You can know more details in this course apart from ISOM 2500.
You can learn the software- Stata which is a fantastic tool for creating regression model and analyzing empirical data.
sections.teaching:
Provide enough examples for each statistic tool.
You can understand all the materials if you are in the class.
sections.grading: Even you get below mean in the midterm, it doesn't matter. As long as you can do well in final, B range is easy to achieve.
sections.workload: Only six assignments, one midterm and one final.

sections.content:
Statistical regression techniques in modelling and estimating economic and business relationships.
Basic knowledge of statistics and regression including linear and non-linear are covered. The focus is simple linear regression.
STATA is also covered and required for homework but not too much.
There are only around four examples throughout the whole textbook. So the prof provided an example himself to help us apply what we've learned into practice (as well as drawing some attention of students...)
sections.teaching:
In most cases, the prof will just repeat what is on the notes and his tone is absolutely matter-of-fact, which makes the classes a little boring. Fortunately, I listened carefully sometimes and once the example he gave was one of the possible answers in the midterm. Going to class and listening to him carefully is therefore important.
The tutorials are even more boring(Peter I'm sorry for that). I together with some friends don't think the TA can explain a problem clearly and briefly. Generally TA will either provides some questions from past paper and work them out with us or goes through what has been mentioned in class, sometimes with new things added though. Those only mentioned in tutorials are not tested of course but may help you get a deeper understanding. Not every week has a tutorial.
sections.grading:
Six homewrok  15%
Midterm           30%
Final                  55%
Only the five homework with highest scores will be counted.
All short questions for midterm and final. Some require proof and giving examples.
The final is cumulative and covers all course materials. Both midterm and final are closed book/note. But one A4 cheat sheet of one side and two sides will be allowed to bring to midterm and final respectively.
sections.workload:
Quite easy. Only homework, midterm and final.
Peter, TA of lots of courses including ECON3334, is really generous when it comes to grading for both homework and exams.
To get a good grade, not too much work is required but understanding is the key to get high scores in midterm and final. Some after-chapter exercises are rather helpful, I personally think, and they are worthwhile trying if you have time.

sections.content: Very trivial and basic concepts related to regression. The course materials only worth 1 credit rather than 4 credits.
sections.teaching: I have no idea. I have skipped almost all of the classes. I think it is time-saving to study the notes on your own.
sections.grading:
20% 4 problem sets
20% midterm
60% final

I got one mark deducted in problem sets.
midterm  above mean less than 1 sd.
final  above mean more than 2 sd.

My mistakes are mostly about calculation.
From my point of view, econometrics should be less rigorous than statistics, but with more reasoning on economic application.
It is meaningless for an econometrics course to put so many points on the correctness of the result. Is it accounting?

So be careful, the calculation worths a lot, double check before you write down the number, although you may think the course is too easy as well.

TA said there would be difficult problems to differentiate A and A+, well you know....I don't think the exams and grading criteria are well designed.
I finally got an A.
sections.workload:
Extremely low workload.
Nothing else to say.

sections.content: Data analysis, estimation and the usage of STATA.
sections.teaching: The lectures are a little bit boring . Listen carefully and take notes. The exam is very easy but be careful about the homework because they are very useful.
sections.grading: Good. But the mean can be very very high and SD can be very very very small. So you need to be very prudential in the exams. Take care :).
sections.workload: Not too much. 4-5 problem sets in total. Sometimes you need to use STATA to finish your homework but the instruction for it is very clear in the notes.

sections.content:
Not too much for an introductory course
Basically a revisit of ISOM 2500 followed by some economic application and due to the nature of econometrics, a higher emphasis on hypothesis testing.

Exam questions can get quite challenging despite the easy assignements and textbook exercise so be sure to look for extra exercise from other materials if you wish to get a better grade.

Not too much covered on using regression software such as SPSS or STATA, some demonstration during class but not actual use is required.
sections.teaching:
Professor's speech can be quite difficult to follow at times.
The pacing is slightly slower and sometimes professor will use half a lecture to repeat what's already taught in last session.

Nonetheless professor is very keen to answer student question and will respond promptly to enquiries. It will be much easier to follow if you ask him question directly and he's very nice to student so don't hesitate if you have any problem.
sections.grading:
slightly above mean for midterm and slightly below mean final, full mark for all assignment. Final grade is B so actually no as bad as other ECON courses which can drop you to C-range if you get below mean.

Same as most ECON courses, no attendance required, however tutorial by Peter can be quite useful since he will give out tips for exams.
sections.workload:
Only 5 assignments throughout the semester, no project or paper so the workload is actually quite light.

Thus most workload actually goes to self-revising during the term if you wish to get a better grade.
